The test image shows a **split stem** with dark brown discoloration of the internal pith/vascular tissue, while the outer stem tissue appears white/intact. This is a classic stem cross-section view.

Key features:
- Stem split lengthwise
- Dark brown/reddish-brown pith internally
- External stem appears relatively intact (white cortex)

Top candidates: **Brown_Stem_Rot** (brown pith when split), **Sudden_Death_Syndrome** (white pith — rules it out), **Charcoal_Rot** (gray + black specks), **Phytophthora** (dark chocolate-brown stem)

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:
This Brown Stem Rot reference shows both the split stem with dark brown pith AND interveinal chlorosis on leaves — very similar to the test image pattern. Let me check a couple more candidates.
I need one more view from a different class to meet the 8-class requirement.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Split stem with very dark brown/reddish-brown internal pith, white outer cortex — classic internal stem cross-section
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Reference (leaf/93) shows exactly this — split stem with dark brown pith. Symptom description confirms "browning of pith and vascular tissue visible when stems are split lengthwise; healthy stems have white pith, BSR-infected stems have brown pith." Perfect match.
- **SDS**: White pith when split — explicitly rules it out
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Gray exterior with black specks — doesn't match
- **Phytophthora**: External chocolate-brown discoloration from soil line — doesn't match
- **Fusarium**: Different pattern (root/stem vascular, external decay)
- **Rhizoctonia**: External reddish-brown canker at soil line — doesn't match

The dark brown pith on a split stem with intact white outer cortex is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Brown Stem Rot.
